newsitem.title: POLAND: Warta bids for PBK bank's two insurers.
newsitem.headline: Warta bids for PBK bank's two insurers.

text.p: Polish insurer Warta SA is interested in buying into two small insurance firms belonging to Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), slated for a public offer this year, Warta's spokesman said on Thursday.

"We have submitted to the finance ministry our application expressing interest in the firms," Zbigniew Augustynowicz told Reuters. By law, major purchases of shares of insurance companies needed the approval of the finance ministry.

The Rzeczpospolita daily said Warta wanted to buy 50 percent stakes in each of the companies -- non-life insurer Towarzystwo Ubezpieczeniowe PBK SA and life insurer PBK Zycie SA, but Warta's spokesman declined to comment on the report.
A source close to the negotiations, which asked not to be named, said the ministry would decide on Warta's application within a week.
Warta, along with three banks, belongs to a consortium which had bid for a majority stake of PBK but the tender, in which South Korean Samsung also took part, was annulled in July.
The government decided to sell the bank in a public offer and not to a strategic investors.
